title: SM+ acquires Princeton Digital Group's Indonesian enterprise data centers
source_used: ET Datacenters (article text read from the page's own embedded data; the plain-text fulltext copy was empty)
key_facts: PT SMPlus Digital Investama (SM+) announced a definitive agreement to acquire the enterprise data centre business in Indonesia of Princeton Digital Group (PDG).
The deal covers five operational data centre facilities in Greater Jakarta, Bandung, Surabaya and Pekanbaru.
After the deal SM+ will operate 31 sites in 25 cities or markets in Indonesia.
Herson Suindah, President Director and Group CEO of SM+ Holdings, calls it an important milestone in building Indonesia's leading home-grown digital infrastructure platform.

PDG's chief operating officer Varoon Raghavan says PDG bought these enterprise-grade sites as part of its 'enter-and-expand' strategy and has since built a hyperscale portfolio of about 400 MW in Indonesia, which will remain its focus (campuses JC2, JC3 and JC4).
UBS AG Singapore Branch was exclusive financial adviser to SM+.
The article gives no price and no completion date.
quote_evidence: PT SMPlus Digital Investama (SM+) announced it has signed a definitive agreement to acquire the enterprise data center business in Indonesia from Princeton Digital Group (PDG).
Following this deal, SM+ will operate 31 sites in 25 cities or markets within Indonesia.
PDG's focus will continue to be on building its hyperscale portfolio, which includes the JC2, JC3, and JC4 campuses, with further expansion underway.
why_it_matters_hint: An Indonesian operator is adding five business data centres while the seller concentrates on very large cloud-scale sites.
